deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

kms_key_name.description:
The resource name of the Cloud KMS CryptoKey to be used to protect access
to messages published on this topic. Your project's PubSub service account
('service-{{PROJECT_NUMBER}}@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com') must have
'roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' to use this feature.
The expected format is 'projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*'
kms_key_name.rationale: Without CMEK, Pub/Sub topics rely on Google-managed encryption. Specifying a customer-managed key gives full control over encryption, supports compliance requirements, and allows key revocation to immediately block data access.

labels.description:
A set of key/value label pairs to assign to this Topic.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are metadata used for organisation and billing; they do not affect access controls, encryption, or other security mechanisms.

message_retention_duration.description:
Indicates the minimum duration to retain a message after it is published
to the topic. If this field is set, messages published to the topic in
the last messageRetentionDuration are always available to subscribers.
For instance, it allows any attached subscription to seek to a timestamp
that is up to messageRetentionDuration in the past. If this field is not
set, message retention is controlled by settings on individual subscriptions.
The rotation period has the format of a decimal number, followed by the
letter 's' (seconds). Cannot be more than 31 days or less than 10 minutes.
message_retention_duration.rationale: Sets how long the topic retains published messages. This is a data-management/retention choice for the team; it is not an access or exposure control and a fixed retention value cannot be generically prescribed.

name.rationale: Topic names are identifiers only and do not control access, encryption, or other security settings.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies the GCP project context for the resource; does not independently control access or security settings.

tags.description:
Input only. Resource manager tags to be bound to the topic. Tag keys and
values have the same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in
the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id}, and values are in the format
tagValues/456. The field is ignored when empty. The field is immutable and
causes resource replacement when mutated. This field is only set at create
time and modifying this field after creation will trigger recreation. To
apply tags to an existing resource, see the 'google_tags_tag_value'
resource.

ingestion_data_source_settings.description: Settings for ingestion from a data source into this topic.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_kines.description: Settings for ingestion from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams.

AWS role ARN to be used for Federated Identity authentication with
Kinesis. Check the Pub/Sub docs for how to set up this role and the
required permissions that need to be attached to it.

The Kinesis consumer ARN to used for ingestion in
Enhanced Fan-Out mode. The consumer must be already
created and ready to be used.
ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_kines.rationale: Identifier (ARN) referencing the AWS Kinesis consumer for enhanced fan-out. It is a team-specific pointer to an external resource; we don't constrain references to other resources.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_kines.description:
The GCP service account to be used for Federated Identity authentication
with Kinesis (via a 'AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity' call for the provided
role). The 'awsRoleArn' must be set up with 'accounts.google.com:sub'
equals to this service account number.
The Kinesis stream ARN to ingest data from.
ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_kines.rationale: Identifier (ARN) referencing the AWS Kinesis stream to ingest from. It is a team-specific pointer to an external resource; we don't constrain references to other resources.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_msk.description: Settings for ingestion from Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_msk.a.description:
AWS role ARN to be used for Federated Identity authentication with
MSK. Check the Pub/Sub docs for how to set up this role and the
required permissions that need to be attached to it.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_msk.c.description: ARN that uniquely identifies the MSK cluster.
ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_msk.c.rationale: Identifier (ARN) referencing the AWS MSK cluster to ingest from. This is a pointer to an external resource that is team-specific; we don't constrain references to other resources.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_msk.g.description:
The GCP service account to be used for Federated Identity authentication
with MSK (via a 'AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity' call for the provided
role). The 'awsRoleArn' must be set up with 'accounts.google.com:sub'
equals to this service account number.

ingestion_data_source_settings.aws_msk.t.description: The name of the MSK topic that Pub/Sub will import from.

ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.description: Settings for ingestion from Azure Event Hubs.
The Azure event hub client ID to use for ingestion.
ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.rationale: Identifier of the Azure AD application used for federated ingestion. It is a reference to an external identity that varies per team; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain it without hardcoding a value.

ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.description: The Azure event hub to ingest data from.
ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.rationale: Identifies the specific event hub to ingest from; does not control authentication or access permissions.

ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.description:
The GCP service account to be used for Federated Identity authentication
with Azure (via a 'AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity' call for the provided
role).
The Azure event hub namespace to ingest data from.
ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.rationale: Identifies the Azure Event Hubs namespace; does not control authentication or access permissions.

ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.description: The name of the resource group within an Azure subscription.
ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.rationale: Identifies the Azure resource group containing the event hub; does not independently control authentication or access.

ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.description: The Azure event hub subscription ID to use for ingestion.
ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.rationale: Identifies the Azure subscription containing the event hub; does not independently control authentication.

ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.description: The Azure event hub tenant ID to use for ingestion.
ingestion_data_source_settings.azure_eve.rationale: Identifier referencing the Azure AD tenant for federated ingestion. It is a team-specific reference to an external directory; a generic policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding a specific tenant.

ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.description: Settings for ingestion from Cloud Storage.

Cloud Storage bucket. The bucket name must be without any
prefix like "gs://". See the bucket naming requirements:
https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/buckets#naming.
ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.rationale: Identifier referencing the source Cloud Storage bucket for ingestion. We don't constrain references to other resources; the bucket's own IAM/config is secured on the bucket, not here.

ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.description:
Glob pattern used to match objects that will be ingested. If unset, all
objects will be ingested. See the supported patterns:
https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/objects/list#list-objects-and-prefixes-using-glob
ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.rationale: Filters objects by name pattern for ingestion scoping; does not affect access controls or authentication.

ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.description:
The timestamp set in RFC3339 text format. If set, only objects with a
larger or equal timestamp will be ingested. Unset by default, meaning
all objects will be ingested.
ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.rationale: Filters objects by creation time for ingestion scoping; does not affect access controls or authentication.

ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.description:
Configuration for reading Cloud Storage data in Avro binary format. The
bytes of each object will be set to the 'data' field of a Pub/Sub message.

Configuration for reading Cloud Storage data written via Cloud Storage
subscriptions(See https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/cloudstorage). The
data and attributes fields of the originally exported Pub/Sub message
will be restored when publishing.

Configuration for reading Cloud Storage data in text format. Each line of
text as specified by the delimiter will be set to the 'data' field of a
Pub/Sub message.

The delimiter to use when using the 'text' format. Each line of text as
specified by the delimiter will be set to the 'data' field of a Pub/Sub
message. When unset, '\n' is used.
ingestion_data_source_settings.cloud_sto.rationale: Controls how text is split into messages during ingestion; does not affect security controls.

ingestion_data_source_settings.confluent.description: Settings for ingestion from Confluent Cloud.
The Confluent Cloud bootstrap server. The format is url:port.
ingestion_data_source_settings.confluent.rationale: Identifies the Confluent Cloud connection endpoint; does not control authentication or access permissions.
Identifies the Confluent Cloud cluster; does not control authentication or access permissions.

ingestion_data_source_settings.confluent.description:
The GCP service account to be used for Federated Identity authentication
with Confluent Cloud.
Identity pool ID to be used for Federated Identity authentication with Confluent Cloud.
ingestion_data_source_settings.confluent.rationale: Identifier referencing the workload identity pool used for Confluent ingestion. It is a team-specific reference to another resource; a generic policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding a value.

ingestion_data_source_settings.confluent.description: Name of the Confluent Cloud topic that Pub/Sub will import from.

ingestion_data_source_settings.platform_.description:
Settings for Platform Logs regarding ingestion to Pub/Sub. If unset,
no Platform Logs will be generated.'

The minimum severity level of Platform Logs that will be written. If unspecified,
no Platform Logs will be written. Default value: "SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED" Possible values: ["SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED", "DISABLED", "DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR"]
ingestion_data_source_settings.platform_.rationale: Setting severity too high (e.g. ERROR only) or leaving it SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED suppresses security-relevant log entries, reducing audit trail coverage for ingestion events.

message_storage_policy.description:
Policy constraining the set of Google Cloud Platform regions where
messages published to the topic may be stored. If not present, then no
constraints are in effect.

message_storage_policy.allowed_persisten.description:
A list of IDs of GCP regions where messages that are published to
the topic may be persisted in storage. Messages published by
publishers running in non-allowed GCP regions (or running outside
of GCP altogether) will be routed for storage in one of the
allowed regions. An empty list means that no regions are allowed,
and is not a valid configuration.
message_storage_policy.allowed_persisten.rationale: Restricts message storage to approved geographic regions, enforcing data residency compliance and preventing sensitive data from being stored in jurisdictions that may not meet regulatory requirements.

message_storage_policy.enforce_in_transi.description:
If true, 'allowedPersistenceRegions' is also used to enforce in-transit
guarantees for messages. That is, Pub/Sub will fail topics.publish
operations on this topic and subscribe operations on any subscription
attached to this topic in any region that is not in 'allowedPersistenceRegions'.
message_storage_policy.enforce_in_transi.rationale: When enabled, prevents message data from transiting through unauthorised regions, strengthening data residency guarantees beyond storage alone.

message_transforms.description:
Transforms to be applied to messages published to the topic. Transforms are applied in the
order specified.

message_transforms.disabled.description:
Controls whether or not to use this transform. If not set or 'false',
the transform will be applied to messages. Default: 'true'.
message_transforms.disabled.rationale: Controls whether the transform is active; the security concern lies in the transform code itself, not in this enable/disable flag.

message_transforms.ai_inference.description:
AI Inference. Specifies the Vertex AI endpoint that inference
requests built from the Pub/Sub message data and provided parameters will
be sent to.

message_transforms.ai_inference.endpoint.description:
The endpoint to a Vertex AI model of the form
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/endpoints/{endpoint}' or
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/{publisher}/models/{model}'.
Vertex AI API requests will be sent to this endpoint.

message_transforms.ai_inference.service_.description:
The service account to use to make prediction requests against
endpoints.

message_transforms.ai_inference.unstruct.description: Configuration for making inferences using arbitrary JSON payloads.

A parameters object to be included in each inference request.
The parameters object is combined with the data field of the Pub/Sub
message to form the inference request.

message_transforms.javascript_udf.description:
Javascript User Defined Function. If multiple Javascript UDFs are specified on a resource,
each one must have a unique 'function_name'.

message_transforms.javascript_udf.code.rationale: Holds the free-form JavaScript UDF body applied to messages. Like a free-form policy document, an arbitrary code blob cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform policy, so it is out of scope.

message_transforms.javascript_udf.functi.description: Name of the JavaScript function that should be applied to Pub/Sub messages.
message_transforms.javascript_udf.functi.rationale: A name identifier for the UDF function; does not itself introduce a security risk.

schema_settings.description: Settings for validating messages published against a schema.

schema_settings.encoding.description: The encoding of messages validated against schema. Default value: "ENCODING_UNSPECIFIED" Possible values: ["ENCODING_UNSPECIFIED", "JSON", "BINARY"]
schema_settings.encoding.rationale: Specifies the serialisation encoding for schema-validated messages; does not affect access controls or encryption.

schema_settings.first_revision_id.description: The minimum (inclusive) revision allowed for validating messages. If empty or not present, allow any revision to be validated against last_revision or any revision created before.

schema_settings.last_revision_id.description: The maximum (inclusive) revision allowed for validating messages. If empty or not present, allow any revision to be validated against first_revision or any revision created after.

schema_settings.schema.description:
The name of the schema that messages published should be
validated against. Format is projects/{project}/schemas/{schema}.
The value of this field will be _deleted-schema_
if the schema has been deleted.
schema_settings.schema.rationale: Identifies the schema for message validation; does not control access or encryption settings.
